source.original_title: 05/20/2026 - Fabrice Schwartz & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/20/2026 - Fabrice Schwartz & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Lost

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: I know you spoke with Kim. He gave me like a little bit of a head start

prospect.name: Fabrice Schwartz
prospect.occupation: Self-directed — 'I'm building a new project, so I take a lot of time'
prospect.family_status: New father to a baby girl, about eighteen months old
prospect.training_background: Four years of kettlebell training, self-directed and inconsistent — 'not choices that very light, it was up and down'. Was in shape until about eighteen months ago; now training roughly twice a week. Says he knows how to train: 'it's not like I need a trainer, I know how to train'.
prospect.medical: Ongoing pain in shoulders, back, elbows and sometimes knees, which he attributes to loss of conditioning. Chronic sleep deprivation since the baby — four to five hours a night in two- and three-hour fragments. No diagnosis, injury history or clinician contact was asked about or disclosed.

signals: Lost ground to a specific hard season — 'a year and a half ago... Baby' and 'I barely work out' — and wants his previous state back
Not deconditioned or naive: four years of kettlebell experience and an articulate model of his own decline ('when you stop, everything degrades and it's a negative')
Counter-signal: he shows no urgency or regret, and frames the trigger as opportunity rather than pain — 'I have the opportunity to do it now, so I guess that's the right time for me'

goals.text: Get back in shape after eighteen months of barely working out
Feel better on a daily basis with more energy
Get out of the shoulder, back, elbow and knee pain he links to lost conditioning
Be pushed harder than he pushes himself and learn approaches he is not currently using

pains.text: Training dropped to twice a week and became inconsistent after the baby arrived
Four to five hours of broken sleep a night, in two- and three-hour blocks
Pain in shoulders, back, elbows and knees
Does not push himself hard enough training alone — 'sometimes you like, don't push enough or you don't go the extra mile'
Time absorbed by a new project he is building alongside the new baby

evidence: The $6,000 / six-month and $9,000 / twelve-month coaching offer was never presented or priced at any point

The rep disqualified him from the coaching in substance and routed him to a different product: 'we have something that's it's $200 a month... I think that's probably what is probably all you need to be honest with you'

Asked directly what was on offer — 'What exactly is the thing you're offering to understand?' — he was told 'Everything is completely tailored' and then immediately shown the $200/month membership instead
No payment taken and no commitment given; the rep texted a self-serve sign-up link and the prospect said 'I'll check it out'
Counter-evidence: the prospect may still self-serve onto the $200/month product, so this is a lost coaching sale rather than a lost relationship
Call ended at twelve minutes with no consequence frame, no commitment check and no financial question of any kind
outcome.next_step: Prospect to review a texted link to the $200/month Skool membership and self-serve sign up in the app if he wants it; no follow-up call proposed by either side

notable.note: The only call in the batch where the core offer was never presented. Twelve minutes in, the rep unilaterally routed an inbound, setter-qualified sales call to a $200/month Skool membership, screen-shared it, texted the link and ended the call. No affordability question was ever asked, so the downsell rests on the rep's read of the prospect rather than on anything the prospect said — he raised no price objection and gave no financial signal at all. Principals should know a $200/month product exists and is being offered on closer calls, and that at least one prospect asked outright what the offer was and never learned the one-to-one coaching existed. A man reporting shoulder, back, elbow and knee pain on four to five hours of broken sleep was sent an unsupervised self-serve kettlebell library with no screening question.

quality.notes: Persistently inverted on short turns. The rep's opening question at 00:00:27 and several follow-ups ('are you doing kettlebells or are you doing something different?', 'I said I have the opportunity to do it now') sit in the prospect's blocks, and the reply to 'How old are you?' is lost inside a swapped exchange, so the prospect's age could not be recovered. The entire Skool pitch from 00:08:51 to 00:12:05 is one unpunctuated run-on block with the prospect's replies embedded inside the rep's turn.
